walkthroughs.body_html:
Hippocrates lived around 460-370 BC.

He told doctors to observe symptoms carefully and let nature heal. His Four Humours theory said health meant keeping blood, phlegm, yellow bile and black bile in balance.

Galen (c.129-216 AD) was a Greek doctor in Rome.

He developed the theory of opposites — treat too much heat with cold. He dissected animals and got some human anatomy wrong, but his books shaped medicine for 1,500 years.

In the Middle Ages the Church taught Galen as fact.

Dissection was rare. Treatments included bloodletting, herbs, prayer and pilgrimage. The Black Death of 1348-49 killed about a third of England's people — yet doctors still blamed miasma and God.
